newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Four Timorese villagers said killed by rebels.
newsitem.headline: Four Timorese villagers said killed by rebels.

text.p: Indonesia's military said four East Timorese villagers found dead in a forest last week were killed by rebels, the official Antara news agency reported on Sunday.
The bodies were found near Cribas village, about 70 km (42 miles) east of the capital, Dili, on Friday by a combined military-civilian search party, the report said.

Lieutenant-Colonel Daud Napis, head of the Manatuto military district, was quoted as saying on Saturday the four had apparently gone hunting after being given permission to enter the forest as part of a funeral procession from a neighbouring village.
The search, delayed because of bad weather, had been called after a member of the group fled after hearing shots fired on Wednesday while in the forest with the four.
Napis said the men had been shot and slashed with machetes. Two had been tied before being killed.
"From the footprints and the way they were killed I am certain the perpetrators were rebels," Napis was quoted as saying.
Indonesia still faces armed resistance to its rule in East Timor which it invaded in December 1975 and unilaterally declared the territory's its 27th province the following year.
The United Nations has never recognised Indonesia's annexation and regards Portugal as being East Timor's administering power.
A number of unexplained killings and disappearances in East Timor had made residents in the territory uneasy in recent months, sources said.
